title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§7 of the notes, continued from the previous page). A stratified space X has closed strata closures X_i indexed by a poset I. A subset I_0 of strata, pairwise disjoint and minimal (the deepest ones), has been chosen. Each β in I_0 carries a closed tube T_β, which is the mapping cylinder C(p_β) of a boundary projection p_β: Ẋ_β → X_β. Set X* = X minus the open tubes; it is stratified by X*_i = X_i ∩ X* for i in I* = I \ I_0. The previous page (18)-(20) recovers X by gluing: X = X* ∐ over Ẋ of the disjoint union of the C(p_β). The X_i are then rebuilt as X*_i together with the cylinders over Ẋ_{i,β} = X*_i ∩ Ẋ_β and with X_β. The remaining transversality conditions are listed there.

This page asks which extra conditions on the 'unfolded' data (18) guarantee two things for the reconstructed X_i: that they are increasing (i ≤ j implies X_i ⊂ X_j), and that the stratification axiom (14) holds, X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k ≤ i,j} X_k.

Step 1, the poset (21). For β in I_0, Grothendieck defines I*_β = {i in I* | i ≥ β}. He observes that the ordered set I with its subset is equivalent to the following data: the poset I*, the bare set I_0, and the family of subsets I*_β ⊂ I* for β in I_0. So I is recovered by gluing an antichain of minimal elements below I*, each attached along an up-set.

Step 2, monotonicity.
- If i = β is in I_0, then X_β ⊂ X_j for j in I*_β by the construction (19), since the cylinder includes its base.
- If i is in I*, monotonicity follows from (19) plus the evident condition (e): i ≤ j in I* implies X*_i ⊂ X*_j.

Step 3, the intersection formula. Condition (f) is the stratification axiom on X*: X*_i ∩ X*_j = ∪_{k ≤ i,j} X*_k. To check X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k ≤ i,j} X_k on X, it suffices to treat incomparable i, j.
- If one of them is β in I_0 and j is in I* \ I*_β, the formula says X_β ∩ X_j = ∅, which again follows from (19).
- The case of two elements of I_0 is covered by the disjointness (20a).
- The case i, j both in I* is done on the next page, by restricting to each tube T_β and using the cylinder structure.

The outcome, on the next page, is a Proposition: stratified spaces with transversal tubular/cylindrical data are equivalent to their 'déploiement' data (X*, boundaries, projections) satisfying (20), (e), (f). This serves the program of reconstructing a stratified space from its unfolding and of defining conical structures (§8).
errors: The claimed equivalence 'données (I ⊃ I*) ⟺ I*, I_0, (I*_β)' tacitly needs three things. Each I*_β must be an up-set (upward closed) in I*, for transitivity. I_0 must be an antichain of minimal elements, which is implicit from the disjoint tubes. Without these stipulations an arbitrary family of subsets does not define an order.

For 'X_β ∩ X_j = ∅ when j ∉ I*_β' to 'follow from (19)', one needs Ẋ_{j,β} = X*_j ∩ Ẋ_β = ∅ for j not ≥ β, or equivalently that (19) only attaches cylinders over those β with j ≥ β. Likewise X_β ⊂ X_j for j ≥ β needs Ẋ_{j,β} to map onto (or at least closure-cover) X_β. These compatibility conditions are used, and are made explicit on the next page as 'X_i ∩ T_β ≠ ∅ i.e. i ∈ I_β', but they are not listed among (e), (f) on this page.
The page writes I_β where I*_β (defined in (21)) is meant, and 'β∈i_0' for 'β∈I_0'. These are notational slips.

ideas.what: Reconstruction of a stratified space by removing open conical tubes around the deepest strata and regluing mapping cylinders ('déploiement'/unfolding), with conditions on the unfolded data equivalent to the stratification axioms
ideas.modern_name: Unfolding / unzipping of stratified spaces; Thom–Mather control data and mapping-cylinder neighborhoods; inductive structure of abstract stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970/2012), Verona (1984), Goresky–MacPherson; 'unzipping' in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches 'déploiement' of stratified spaces and tame topology in outline only; the detailed verification is not published

ideas.what: Decomposition of the stratification poset I as I* plus an antichain I_0 of minimal elements, each attached along the up-set I*_β ⊂ I*
ideas.modern_name: Poset gluing / up-set (cosieve) description of the link poset; exit-path category stratum-by-stratum induction
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard combinatorics of posets; used implicitly in Lurie HA Appendix A, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Conditions (e), (f): the restricted strata X*_i form a stratification of the complement of the tubes, plus disjointness checks for incomparable pairs
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition verification for restricted stratification

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping verifying that the poset structure and the frontier condition survive the cut-and-reglue (unfolding) construction. The overall program is known from the Esquisse, and the technique matches Thom–Mather/Verona. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'la condition (19)' should read 'la condition (14)'. The image shows (14), the frontier condition X_i∩X_j=∪X_k.
'(I ⊃ I')' is plausibly '(I ⊃ I*)' in context. The marginal note '(I ens. ordonné)' sits above it.
'β∈i_0' should be 'β ∈ I_0'. 'i∈I*\I_β' should be 'j ∈ I* \ I*_β', matching the conclusion X_β ∩ X_j = ∅.
'compte tenu de la condition mise [?] évidente' should likely read 'compte tenu de la condition suivante évidente'.
In the marginal note '(donc j∈I*)', the word 'donc' is uncertain. It may be '(dans I*)'.
'clair par (19)' may read 'clair sur (19)' in the image. This makes no difference to the meaning.
